the spatial distribution and energy of frontier orbitals can be tailored by changing the peripheral groups in salen-based metal complexes and that the self-assembled nanostructures can be controlled by tuning the nature of these substituents.

the self-assembled structures of the Ni(II) salen complexes are affected by the nature of peripheral functional groups, which tune the dipole moment of the molecules and, therefore, the 2D packing of the nanoarchitectures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of 2D self-assembled nanostructures based on salen-type building blocks.
the synthesis, electronic structure and self-assembling behavior of a series of salen complexes with carboxylic acid substituents.
the design and synthesis of new building blocks for the construction of nanoarchitectures, which is an important step towards the fabrication of molecular devices with specific functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 2D nanostructures of the three salen complexes are stabilized by the hydrogen bonding between the carboxylic acid and amine groups, while the nature of the diamine bridge and tert-butyl substituents affects the 2D packing.

, for the three complexes studied, the 2D self-assembly process is driven by the nature of their substituents, while the 1D self-assembly is controlled by the hydrogen bonding between the carboxylic acid groups of the salen ligand and the water molecules of the solvent.
the nature of the peripheral groups of the ligand and of the diamine bridge can be used to tune the 2D packing of Ni(II)-salen building blocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to tune the 2D packing of the self-assembled nano-objects by using different substituents on the organic ligand.

by changing the substituents of the salen ligands, the spatial distribution of LUMOs and HOMOs can be controlled, and this will affect the intermolecular interactions, leading to the formation of different nanoarchitectures.
the nature of the 2D self-assembled nanostructure can be tuned by the substituents of the organic ligands of Ni(II )-salen-based building blocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-assembly of the Ni(II) complexes into 2D nanostructures can be tuned by the nature and the position of the substituets, which is confirmed by the DFT calculations and the STM experiments.
it is possible to tune the 2D packing and the electronic structure of self-assembled 2D architectures by changing the nature of the peripheral substituents.
the structure of the 2D nanoassemblies of these building blocks is governed by the nature of their substituents.
